title: Every operation of the product through one bridge, in place of hand-made wrappers
request: The owner (2026-10-25): DCLab Code, a minimal developer app like Claude Code and Codex, must carry every capability of the R&D project behind its chat: "all agentic systems we designed work behind the chat, as Claude's or Codex's do"; then "most things are available: implement, adopt and integrate them, no need to make them again"; "the main repo" is this R&D repository (Research_Development_DCLab), not the main product repository.
plan: list the app's operations from its own OpenAPI description
run one inside the same app with the page's checks
keep long results in the workspace

decisions.decision: Seven planned wrappers (workspace_ask, evidence_ask, solution_report, lineage, programme_view, lessons, notebook_review) replaced by dclab_capabilities + dclab_call over the 174 operations: nothing copied, the list grows with the product (the owner: adopt, never rebuild).
decisions.why: the owner: adopt and integrate, never rebuild; the API grows and the bridge follows it

decisions.decision: The local owner's request token without sign-in, the caller's API token with it (an AUTHORIZATION contextvar from the MCP request), so each route checks the role as for any request.
decisions.why: each route checks its own role; the bridge adds no second permission system

decisions.decision: The person's own switches are refused whatever the caller: a chat's model never flips routing, sign-in, members, budgets, consent, the twin or team switches.
decisions.why: those switches belong to the person or the owner, audited on their pages

decisions.decision: Writes through the bridge run only from an allow-list of agent work and proposals (AGENT_WRITES, by route template, with body keys that stay the person's); every other write is refused, and reads run except rows, data files and streams
decisions.why: a block list of the person's operations missed approvals, gate policy, labels and builds (review 2); the routes record their writes as the person's and their stage runs as a human's move, so a write not proven to be agent work must stay the person's

decisions.decision: Each call is judged by the operation it reaches (the most specific template of the app's own API description), never by the raw path; a path with %-escapes, #, ? or // is refused
decisions.why: the app routes the decoded path without its fragment: /api/%63onsent reached the consent switch

change: chat_agents.dclab_capabilities, dclab_call, _request/_route, _keep; services.app set by create_app; mcp_server passes the Authorization header.

findings.defect: the capabilities tests ran the Home tests twice
findings.scenario: the capabilities class inherited the Home test class

findings.defect: a tool outside the recording functions failed the harness test
findings.scenario: test_agent_harness's TOOL_CALLERS whitelist did not know the chat dispatch
findings.cause: a new call site of the registry

findings.defect: the person's switches were reachable with %-escapes or a # fragment
findings.scenario: dclab_call PUT /api/%63onsent {use: train, on: true} returned 200 and flipped the workspace's training consent; /api/twin/settings%73 and /api/team/settings# turned those switches on
findings.cause: the refusal matched the raw path string; the app routes the decoded path without the fragment
findings.fix: refuse %, #, ?, // in the path; judge the operation's template from the API description

findings.defect: the chat could approve gates, switch off the holdout approval and set a project's consent, recorded as the person's
findings.scenario: POST /api/projects/{id}/approvals {gate: solution}, PATCH /api/projects/{id} {policy: {require_holdout_approval: false}}, PATCH ... {settings: {consent: {train: true}}} each returned 200; the audit wrote approve_gate, set_policy, set_consent with actor human
findings.cause: a block list of the person's operations; the routes record 'human' and tell the graph validator the actor is human
findings.fix: an allow-list of agent writes; the audit records any route run during an MCP call as the agent's

findings.defect: raw table rows reached the external model, the call log and the store
findings.scenario: dclab_call GET /api/drafts/{d}/assets/{a}/rows returned unmasked rows (the route's own docstring: never sent to a model), kept whole in mcp/calls.jsonl; /download saved the CSV
findings.fix: reads of rows, downloads, code/notebook/sft exports, trial files and streams refused

findings.defect: writes through the bridge were recorded as the person's own choices
findings.scenario: PUT /api/drafts/{d}/solution became a correction with source person and a ledger capture of the person's choice; decide/choose, ledger blind labels and feedback were open
findings.fix: those writes are refused (not agent work); audit.record turns 'human' into the agent's during an MCP call

findings.defect: every chat tool crashed in a second workspace
findings.scenario: with accounts on, a token for another workspace called home_start: AttributeError 'Services' object has no attribute 'app'
findings.cause: Pool._open copied csrf and build_from_chat to a new workspace's services, not app
findings.test: (code; accounts mode is not covered by a test)

findings.defect: one stream route could hold a chat for 10 minutes
findings.scenario: dclab_call GET /api/drafts/{id}/events streams up to 600 s and the MCP call waited
findings.fix: /events refused with the other reads that never reach a chat

findings.defect: the chat could make the person's 'drop a part' decision
findings.scenario: the solution team paused on drop:<block>; dclab_call POST /api/projects/X/team {answer: 'drop it, no data'} ran programme.drop as 'human', past the validator's 'only a person drops a leaf', recorded as the person's in four places
findings.cause: the allow-list kept only 'approve' as the person's part of the team walk

findings.defect: the chat could wipe the person's map edits and confirmation
findings.scenario: after the person confirmed the map on the page, dclab_call POST /api/drafts/D/map {redraw: true} dropped the confirmation, recorded as the person's redraw
findings.cause: the map route was allowed without its person keys

findings.defect: allowed routes still wrote experience events as the person's
findings.scenario: job.stopped and decision.proposed (a what-if) recorded actor person during an MCP call
findings.cause: only the audit relabelled the actor
findings.fix: experience.record turns 'person' into 'agent' during an MCP call, except chat.person, draft.created and visit.started (the person's relayed words, marked surface mcp)
findings.test: tests/test_chat_agents.py (no person event in a chat's calls)

findings.defect: a '.' path segment was judged as one route and sent as another
findings.scenario: POST /api/drafts/./map judged /api/drafts/{draft_id}/map, sent as /api/drafts/map (httpx drops dot segments); 49 such pairs, none reaching a refused operation today

measurements.name: bridge tests
measurements.gate: the bridge lists more than 150 operations, keeps a route's own status, refuses every person's switch
measurements.result: 174 operations listed; a 422 kept; consent, routing, tokens and the twin switch refused

outcome: A chat reaches every operation of the R&D product (drafts, projects, stages, decisions, lineage, lessons, reports, jobs, the intern, the teams, the twin) with the page's checks.
lessons: An API description is already the tool list: search it instead of hand-writing wrappers.
risks: an operation's description is only as good as its docstring; some operations may need better summaries for a chat to pick them
